ideas.name: Candidate Follow-Up Desk
ideas.product: A lightweight queue that shows which candidates need a response, what was promised, and when a recruiter should follow up.
ideas.audience: independent recruiters and boutique recruiting firms
ideas.problem: Candidate communication is spread across email, LinkedIn, calendars, and ATS notes, so promised updates are easy to miss.
ideas.valueProposition: Turns candidate follow-up into a visible queue with owners, next dates, outcomes, and stop conditions.
ideas.topic: candidate follow-up tracking for recruiting agencies
ideas.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
ideas.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
ideas.seoAngle: Targets candidate follow-up spreadsheet, recruiter follow-up template, candidate communication tracker, and recruiting CRM reminder searches.

probeContext.outcome: every active candidate receives the promised next update or a documented closed reason
workflow: Capture the communication promise
Set the next-contact date
Send the contextual update
Record the response
Close or schedule the next step
mistakes: Recording messages without a next-contact date
Sending generic check-ins with no useful update
Continuing reminders after a candidate withdraws
Keeping ownership implicit when a role changes hands

metrics.name: Promise kept rate
metrics.formula: promised updates delivered on time / promised updates due

metrics.name: Open follow-up age
metrics.formula: current date - oldest unresolved next-contact date

metrics.name: Response outcome mix
metrics.formula: count by advanced, waiting, declined, or no response

alternatives.name: Recruiter inbox, LinkedIn reminders, and calendar tasks
alternatives.best: One owner handles low volume and can see every open item
alternatives.limit: Status and follow-up history depend on memory and inbox searches

alternatives.name: ATS tasks or a shared candidate follow-up spreadsheet
alternatives.best: The team already maintains it and exceptions are simple
alternatives.limit: Purpose-built reminders, evidence, and stop conditions require manual setup

alternatives.name: A focused workflow tool
alternatives.best: The same coordination failure repeats across many live records
alternatives.limit: It must integrate with the system of record and justify another workflow

triggers: a promised update date passes without a logged message
a candidate replies with a question or changed availability
a role is paused, filled, or reassigned
examples: A shortlisted candidate was promised feedback Friday but the client has not responded
A passive candidate asks to reconnect after a compensation review
A recruiter leaves and twenty active conversations need a new owner
rules: A reminder must stop when the candidate or role closes
Every message should communicate a real status or next decision
The ATS remains the candidate system of record
Sensitive candidate details should not be copied into unnecessary tools

ideas.name: Search Intake Scorecard
ideas.product: A structured client-intake and calibration record for boutique recruiters opening a new search.
ideas.audience: independent recruiters and boutique recruiting firms
ideas.problem: Recruiters start sourcing with vague or conflicting requirements, then lose time recalibrating after weak candidate submissions.
ideas.valueProposition: Makes must-haves, tradeoffs, evidence, interview ownership, and calibration decisions explicit before sourcing scales.
ideas.topic: recruiting search intake and candidate calibration scorecards
ideas.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
ideas.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
ideas.seoAngle: Targets recruiting intake form, job intake meeting checklist, candidate scorecard template, and recruiter calibration questions.

probeContext.outcome: the recruiter and client can evaluate the same candidate evidence against the same explicit tradeoffs
workflow: Capture the business outcome
Separate must-haves from preferences
Define evidence and disqualifiers
Calibrate on sample profiles
Approve the search brief
mistakes: Treating every preference as mandatory
Using adjectives that cannot be evaluated
Skipping compensation and location boundaries
Changing criteria after submissions without logging the decision

metrics.name: Calibration change count
metrics.formula: criteria changes after sourcing begins

metrics.name: Submission acceptance rate
metrics.formula: candidates advanced / candidates submitted
metrics.decision: test whether recruiter and client are aligned

metrics.name: Decision turnaround
metrics.formula: decision timestamp - submission timestamp

alternatives.name: A kickoff call followed by recruiter notes
alternatives.best: One owner handles low volume and can see every open item
alternatives.limit: Status and follow-up history depend on memory and inbox searches

alternatives.name: ATS job fields, forms, or a shared intake document
alternatives.best: The team already maintains it and exceptions are simple
alternatives.limit: Purpose-built reminders, evidence, and stop conditions require manual setup

alternatives.name: A focused workflow tool
alternatives.best: The same coordination failure repeats across many live records
alternatives.limit: It must integrate with the system of record and justify another workflow

triggers: two sample profiles receive conflicting evaluations
the client adds a new requirement after sourcing starts
submitted candidates wait beyond the agreed feedback window
examples: A founder says they need a strategic operator but screens only for a specific title
Two interviewers disagree about whether industry experience is mandatory
The compensation ceiling excludes every approved sample profile
rules: Criteria must describe observable evidence
Tradeoffs belong in the brief before sourcing volume increases
Every post-launch change needs an owner and reason
The client approves the scorecard, not just the job description

ideas.name: Interview Debrief Collector
ideas.product: A focused workflow for collecting independent interviewer feedback before the hiring discussion drifts into group consensus.
ideas.audience: independent recruiters and boutique recruiting firms
ideas.problem: Interview feedback arrives late, lacks evidence, or is shaped by the loudest interviewer, delaying client decisions and weakening candidate communication.
ideas.valueProposition: Collects structured evidence, decision confidence, and follow-up questions before a time-boxed debrief.
ideas.topic: interview feedback collection and hiring debrief workflows
ideas.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
ideas.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
ideas.seoAngle: Targets interview feedback form, hiring debrief template, interviewer scorecard, and late feedback reminder searches.

probeContext.outcome: the client reaches an evidence-based candidate decision while the interview is still fresh
workflow: Assign evaluation areas
Collect independent feedback
Flag missing evidence
Run the debrief
Record the decision and candidate update
mistakes: Collecting only an overall rating
Letting interviewers see peers' opinions before submitting
Accepting personality labels without evidence
Holding the candidate update until every minor note is perfect

metrics.name: Feedback completion time
metrics.formula: feedback timestamp - interview end

metrics.name: Evidence completeness
metrics.formula: evaluations with evidence / evaluations due

metrics.name: Decision cycle time
metrics.formula: decision timestamp - final interview end

alternatives.limit: Status and follow-up history depend on memory and inbox searches

alternatives.name: ATS scorecards or a shared interview feedback form
alternatives.best: The team already maintains it and exceptions are simple
alternatives.limit: Purpose-built reminders, evidence, and stop conditions require manual setup

alternatives.name: A focused workflow tool
alternatives.best: The same coordination failure repeats across many live records
alternatives.limit: It must integrate with the system of record and justify another workflow

triggers: an interviewer has not submitted before the debrief cutoff
two evaluations conflict on the same criterion
a concern has no supporting example or follow-up question
examples: A technical interviewer rates low confidence but provides no observed evidence
A panel splits on client-facing ability and needs one targeted follow-up
The final interviewer submits notes after the recruiter already promised an update
rules: Independent feedback is captured before group discussion
Evidence is separated from conclusions
Missing feedback has a cutoff and escalation owner
The final decision includes the candidate communication owner

ideas.name: Maintenance Triage Board
ideas.product: A lightweight intake and routing queue for maintenance requests across a small rental portfolio.
ideas.audience: independent residential property managers and small property teams
ideas.problem: Maintenance requests arrive through calls, texts, email, and tenant portals with inconsistent details, making urgency and ownership hard to assess.
ideas.valueProposition: Standardizes request evidence, urgency, access, vendor ownership, tenant updates, and completion confirmation.
ideas.monetization: $19-$79/month based on active records or team size
ideas.startupCost: Static product probe, managed database, email integration, and lightweight scheduled jobs.
ideas.seoAngle: Targets maintenance request triage template, landlord maintenance tracker, property manager work order spreadsheet, and tenant repair intake searches.

probeContext.outcome: every request has enough evidence for a clear priority, owner, tenant update, and verified resolution
workflow: Capture the request
Assess urgency and missing evidence
Assign an owner or vendor
Coordinate access and updates
Verify completion
mistakes: Assigning a vendor before collecting usable evidence
Using urgent as a catch-all priority
Failing to record access constraints
Closing when the vendor says done without tenant or manager confirmation

metrics.name: Time to triage
metrics.formula: priority-set timestamp - request-received timestamp

metrics.name: Reopen rate
metrics.formula: reopened requests / completed requests

metrics.name: Tenant update compliance
metrics.formula: requests updated by promised time / updates due

triggers: the request mentions water, electrical, security, heat, or another safety signal
required photos or access details are missing
a vendor misses the scheduled window or reports a changed scope
examples: A tenant texts a blurry photo of water under a sink after business hours
A vendor cannot enter because access instructions were never confirmed
A repair is marked complete but the tenant reports the symptom returned
rules: Local emergency and legal requirements remain outside the tool's automated judgment
Urgency decisions require a reason and reviewer
Tenants receive a clear next-update time

ideas.name: Unit Turnover Runbook
